chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Habib narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Barqi, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from Ali (peace be upon him).

That a Magian woman embraced Islam before her husband. Ali (peace be upon him) said: 'Does she embrace Islam?' He said: 'No.' So he separated them. Then he said: 'If she embraces Islam before the expiration of her waiting period, she is your wife; but if her waiting period expires before she embraces Islam, and then you embrace Islam, you are a suitor among suitors.'
ai.seo_question: What happens to the marriage of a Magian couple if the wife converts to Islam before her husband?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq, transmitted through the chain of al-Sakuni, clarifies the fiqh of 'Ikhtilaf al-Din' (difference in religion) within the context of the Hanafi and Shia schools regarding the status of the 'Ahl al-Kitab' spouse. It establishes that the wife's conversion triggers an immediate conditional separation, where the marriage persists only if the husband converts before the completion of her 'iddah', thereby preserving the marital bond through a grace period for his potential acceptance. This ruling underscores the principle that Islam is the foundation of the marital contract, and its absence in one party dissolves the union unless rectified promptly.
